bug_info.bug_desc: In heartbeat mode, the 17-bit step computation produces dc_wrap when the next duty-cycle value crosses the 16-bit boundary. The old code had two related problems. First, the direction-turn logic used the delayed pulse dc_htbt_end_q in the dc_wrap branches, so for typical blink_param_x_i values the wrap condition is not observed on the same update edge and htbt_direction fails to reverse at the boundary. Second, duty_cycle_htbt was assigned directly from dc_htbt_q, so the low 16-bit wrapped residue appeared on the output during a wrapped step interval instead of being clamped to 16'hffff or 0 as required by the heartbeat spec.
bug_info.fix_hint: Latch dc_wrap into a new dc_wrap_q register on the heartbeat step boundary so the wrap is remembered for the entire output step interval. In the direction-turn logic, use the current dc_htbt_end pulse instead of the delayed dc_htbt_end_q so the direction reverses when the step actually crosses the target boundary. Finally, when dc_wrap_q is set, override duty_cycle_htbt to the appropriate clamp value: 16'hffff for a positive overflow and 0 for a negative underflow; otherwise pass dc_htbt_q through.
